info.title: TDEI Gateway Stage API
info.description: This is an API for interacting with the Transportation Data Equity Initiative (TDEI) data system. It is intended for applications producing data to and consuming data from the TDEI system. It currently supports GTFS-Pathways, GTFS-Flex v2 and OpenSidewalks v0.2 data schemas.

post.summary: Authenticates the user with the TDEI system.
post.description: Authenticates the user with the TDEI system using username and password. Returns an access token and refresh token if successfully authenticated. An optional `client_id` may be provided to select a specific auth server client; when omitted, the system default client is used.

200.description: Authentication successful - Returns the access token for the user.

400.description: Password does not satisfiy with password policy.

401.description: Authentication failed - Check username and password.

404.description: User not found.

post.summary: Re-issue an access token
post.description: Re-issues an access token when a valid refresh token is sent to the server. An optional `client_id` may be provided to select a specific auth server client; when omitted, the system default client is used. The `client_id` should match the client used when the original tokens were issued.

200.description: Successful validation of refresh token - Returns the refreshed access token.

401.description: Invalid or expired refresh token provided.

post.summary: Regenerates the API key for the user.
post.description: Regenerates the API key for the user. The old API key will be invalidated and a new API key will be generated.

200.description: Regeneration of API key successful - Returns the new API key.

401.description: Unauthenticated request. Check your access token.

get.description: Starts the Single Sign-On (SSO) login flow by redirecting the browser to the auth server authorization endpoint. The caller must supply a `redirect_uri` that is already registered as a valid redirect URL for the auth server client. After the user authenticates with the auth server, the auth server redirects the browser back to that `redirect_uri` with an authorization `code` and `state` query parameters. The frontend should then call `POST /api/v1/sso-login` with those values to complete login and obtain TDEI access and refresh tokens. An optional `client_id` may be provided to select a specific auth server client; when omitted, the system default client is used.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Frontend callback URL where the auth server will redirect after successful authentication. Must be registered with the auth server for the selected client.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Auth server client id used for the SSO flow. Optional; defaults to the configured default client id when not provided.

302.description: Redirect to the auth server authorization endpoint. Follow the Location header to continue the SSO login flow.

Location.description: Auth server authorization endpoint URL including client, redirect_uri, state, and other OIDC parameters.

400.description: Invalid redirect_uri. The provided redirect_uri is missing, malformed, or not registered with the auth server for the selected client.

post.summary: Complete SSO login
post.description: Completes the Single Sign-On (SSO) login flow by exchanging the authorization `code` and `state` returned from the auth server for TDEI access and refresh tokens. Call this endpoint after the browser is redirected back to the frontend `redirect_uri` from `GET /api/v1/sso-redirect`. The server validates the `state`, exchanges the authorization code with the auth server, and returns a `TokenResponse` that can be used with subsequent authenticated TDEI API requests. The returned tokens follow the same format as the username/password authenticate and refresh-token APIs.

200.description: Successful response - Returns access and refresh tokens.

401.description: Invalid code or state. The authorization code could not be exchanged, the state is invalid or expired, or SSO authentication failed.

get.description: Starts the Single Sign-On (SSO) logout flow by redirecting the browser to the auth server logout endpoint. The caller must supply a `redirect_uri` that is already registered as a Valid post logout redirect URI for the auth server client. After the auth server completes logout, it redirects the browser back to that `redirect_uri`. An optional `client_id` may be provided to select a specific auth server client; when omitted, the system default client is used. The frontend should clear any locally stored TDEI access and refresh tokens after initiating logout.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Frontend URL where the auth server will redirect after logout completes. Must be registered with the auth server as a Valid post logout redirect URI for the selected client.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Auth server client id used for the SSO logout flow. Optional; defaults to the configured default client id when not provided.

302.description: Redirect to the auth server logout endpoint. Follow the Location header to continue the SSO logout flow.

Location.description: Auth server logout endpoint URL including client, post_logout_redirect_uri, and related OIDC logout parameters.

400.description: Invalid redirect_uri. The provided redirect_uri is missing, malformed, or not registered with the auth server as a Valid post logout redirect URI for the selected client.

get.summary: Lists the TDEI datasets in the system.
get.description: This API returns filtered and sorted lists of TDEI datasets.  All text parameters x return datasets with attribute containing x, as opposed to exact match. By default results will include all datasets in released status AND all dataset in pre-release status within the requesting user's project group. This behavior can be controlled by the status parameter.  In no situation can a user see pre-release datasets from a project group the user is not part of.  Primary use cases include: name search: Given a search string X, return all datasets with a name that contains the search string X) dataset id lookup: Given a tdei_dataset_id, return the dataset with the matching id bounding box: Given xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, return datasets with dataset_area overlapping the bounding box Sorting:  Users can sort datasets by 'valid_to', 'valid_from', 'uploaded date', 'project group name', and 'status'.

parameters.description: Type of the dataset. Filters datasets by matching the exact value from the supported enumeration.

parameters.name: status

post.summary: Clones the provided dataset to the designated project group and service.
post.description: Cloning of a dataset lets one to use the dataset being cloned as the base for a new dataset without having to upload the dataset. This operation clones the datafiles in the dataset `tdei_dataset_id` to the designated project group `tdei_project_group_id` and service `tdei_service_id`, and uses the metadata file provided along with the API as the metadata. Returns cloned dataset id if the action is successful.

post.summary: Upload a OSW dataset.
post.description: This endpoint enables users to upload an OSW dataset. The request must include the required parameters to complete the upload. The response includes a `job_id` for tracking the request.To check the request status, refer to the location header in the response, which provides the URL for the status API endpoint. By default, the dataset's status will be set to 'pre-release.' The dataset can be published using the `/publish` endpoint.

parameters.name: tdei_project_group_id
parameters.description: Project group id to which the dataset would be uploaded

parameters.name: tdei_service_id
parameters.description: TDEI service id associated with the above project group id.

parameters.name: derived_from_dataset_id
parameters.description: Dataset id from which this dataset was derived.

dataset.description: OSW file which is expected to be a zip file, internally has {nodes, edges, points}.geojson. If the extensions are present, then the zip file will have {nodes, edges, points}.extension.geojson files

metadata.description: Metadata information for the OSW dataset. This is a JSON file that includes details on how and when the data was collected, the file's valid dates, and other relevant information about the dataset. For more details, refer to the [metadata schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TaskarCenterAtUW/TDEI-osw-datasvc-ts/stage/schema/metadata.schema.json).

changeset.description: The changeset file records modifications to the sidewalk network included in the OSW dataset. It supports file formats with either .zip or .osc extensions.

403.description: User unauthorized to upload the dataset.

For example entities like Footway, Crossing, and Sidewalk have tags such as surface, width, incline, and length, indicating attributes like the material, size, slope, and distance. Returns the tag quality metric for the dataset element tags.

post.summary: Unions two OSW datasets into one connected dataset.
post.description:
Combines two OpenSidewalks (OSW) datasets into **one new dataset**. Features that describe the same real-world thing are merged into one, everything else from both datasets is kept, and the two pedestrian networks are **connected wherever they meet** so the result stays routable.

The request returns a `job_id` straight away; the union runs in the background (see *Tracking the job* below).

---

## 1. Dataset order matters

| Parameter | Role |
|---|---|
| `tdei_dataset_id_one` (**DS1**) | The **base, authoritative** dataset. Its positions, geometry, IDs and attribute values win whenever the two datasets disagree. |
| `tdei_dataset_id_two` (**DS2**) | The dataset **merged into** the base. It fills gaps: new features are added, and attribute keys DS1 does not have are copied across. |

Swapping the two IDs gives a different result.

---

## 2. Two kinds of behaviour

| | What it does | Controlled by `entity_filters`? |
|---|---|---|
| **Connecting** | Joins nodes, splits edges and creates shared nodes so that DS1 and DS2 form one connected network. | **No — always runs.** |
| **Merging** | Removes duplicate features and merges attributes onto the surviving feature. | **Yes.** With no filters, every feature is eligible. |

**Guiding rule: filters decide what is merged, never what is connected.** Routability always comes first. In OSW two edges are connected only when they share a node, so a filter that blocked a node from joining would cut the network at that point.

---

## 3. `proximity`

- Distance in **metres**. **Optional — defaults to `0.5` m when omitted.** Must be greater than 0.
- Measured as true ground distance, the same in every direction and at any latitude.
- Decides:
  - which DS2 node joins which DS1 node;
  - which DS1 node splits a DS2 edge running past it;
  - where a DS2 edge ending beside a DS1 edge is joined to it (T-junctions);
  - which DS1 and DS2 **points** are treated as the same point.
- It is also the default corridor for **edge and line duplicate detection**, unless `duplicate_buffer_width` is set (see section 6).

Choosing a value: too small and genuine gaps between the datasets stay disconnected; too large and nearby but separate features (for example two parallel sidewalks) may be joined. Values of about 0.5–1 m suit data authored to the same base map; 2–3 m suits data collected independently.

---

## 4. Default behaviour — no `entity_filters`

Every feature is eligible to merge. Each file type is compared only with the same file type in the other dataset.

| File type | DS1 and DS2 features are treated as the same when… | Result when they are the same | Result otherwise |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Node** | the DS2 node is within `proximity` of a DS1 node on the same kind of way (a sidewalk node never joins a road node — see section 5) | One node, with the DS1 ID and position. DS2 attribute keys that DS1 lacks are added. **Every** DS2 value (including overridden ones) is recorded in `ext:union_audit_<key>`. Confidence tags are added. | DS2 node added as a new node. |
| **Edge** | the DS2 edge joins the same two nodes as a DS1 edge, **or** at least **80%** of its length lies inside the duplicate corridor of DS1 edges of the **same kind** (sidewalk with sidewalk, crossing with crossing, road with road), and it runs **alongside** them (within 30°) | DS2 edge dropped; the DS1 edge is kept. DS2 edge attributes are **not** copied onto the DS1 edge. | DS2 edge added, its ends connected to the network. |
| **Zone** | the two zones share more than **70%** of the DS1 zone's area | DS1 zone kept; DS2 zone dropped. DS2 zone attributes are **not** merged. | Both zones kept. |
| **Point** | the DS2 point is within `proximity` of a DS1 point of the **same type** (same identifying tag, e.g. `amenity=bench`) | One point, with the DS1 position. DS2-only keys are added; every DS2 value is recorded in `ext:union_audit_<key>`. | DS2 point added. |
| **Line** | at least **70%** of the DS2 line's length lies inside the duplicate corridor of a DS1 line | DS1 line kept; DS2-only keys are added. | DS2 line added. |
| **Polygon** | the polygons intersect | Shared area **more than 70%** of the DS1 polygon: DS1 polygon kept, DS2-only keys added. Shared area **70% or less**: the two shapes are **combined into one polygon** (DS1 ID, DS1 values plus DS2-only keys). | No intersection: both kept. |

Attribute rule used everywhere a merge happens: **DS1 values are never overwritten; DS2 only adds keys DS1 does not have.**

The thresholds above are defaults and can be changed per file type (section 6).

---

## 5. What always happens, whatever the filters

These steps turn DS1 and DS2 into **one routable network**. They run on every request, with or without `entity_filters`. A filter cannot switch them off or narrow them.

| # | Step | What happens | What you see in the output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Node joining** | Each DS2 node joins the nearest DS1 node within `proximity`, provided both lie on the same kind of way. A sidewalk node never joins a road node, and a living-street node joins only another living-street node. **Two nodes at exactly the same coordinate always join**, whatever they lie on. **Two kerb nodes (`barrier=kerb`) never join each other** unless they are at exactly the same coordinate — two kerbs close together are usually opposite sides of a crossing. | One node with the DS1 ID and DS1 position. Every DS2 edge that used the DS2 node now ends on the DS1 node. |
| 2 | **Splitting DS2 edges at DS1 nodes** | A DS1 node lying within `proximity` of the middle of a DS2 edge of the same kind splits that DS2 edge, so the DS1 node can be reached from it. | The DS2 edge appears as two or more pieces that meet at the DS1 node. |
| 3 | **Road × crossing nodes** | Wherever a road and a crossing cross — within one dataset or across the two — both are split at one shared node. If a node already sits exactly at that point, it is reused; otherwise a new node is created. | The road and the crossing each appear in pieces. A new node has an ID beginning `ixn-` and carries the crossing's tags as `ext:osw_*` and the road's tags as `ext:road_*`. **DS1 roads and crossings can be split by this step.** |
| 4 | **T-junctions** | Where a DS2 edge ends within `proximity` of the middle of a DS1 edge, meeting it at 30° or more, the DS1 edge is split at that point and the DS2 edge end is moved onto it. Edges running alongside a DS1 edge are duplicates, not junctions, and are not split. Roads are never split by this step. | The DS1 edge appears in two pieces joined to the DS2 edge. The DS2 edge end may have moved by up to `proximity`. **DS1 edges other than roads can be split by this step.** |
| 5 | **Endpoint alignment** | Every DS2 edge end is moved to the exact position of the node it connects to. The rest of the edge's shape is unchanged. | Each edge's first and last coordinates equal its `_u_id` and `_v_id` nodes exactly. |
| 6 | **Protecting connections during duplicate removal** | A DS2 edge that qualifies as a duplicate is still **kept** when both its ends are nodes on the DS1 network (it is then the link between them), or when removing it would cut off another edge attached to it. The second check repeats along a chain of edges until nothing more would be cut off. | Some DS2 edges that look like duplicates of DS1 edges remain in the output. This is intended: removing them would disconnect the network. |
| 7 | **Removing unused nodes** | Nodes not used by any edge or zone are removed. | No stray nodes. A DS2 node whose only edge was removed as a duplicate does not appear. |

### How these steps interact with filters

- **A filter can stop a feature being removed or having its attributes merged. It cannot stop the feature being joined, split or moved.**
- A DS2 edge that fails the edge filter is always kept, but steps 1–5 still apply to it: its ends can move onto DS1 nodes and it can be split. It comes out **modified, not untouched**.
- Node **joining** ignores filters; node **attribute merging** follows them. Under a sidewalk-only edge filter, a DS2 crossing node still joins its DS1 node, but its attributes are recorded only in `ext:union_audit_*`.

### What can change in DS1

- **DS1 nodes never move.** DS1 attribute values are never overwritten; merges only add keys DS1 lacks.
- **DS1 edges are changed only by steps 3 and 4**, and only by being split. Their shape is kept: the split point lies on the original line.

---

## 6. `entity_filters` — optional

**Omitted:** every feature of every file type is eligible to merge, exactly as in section 4.

**Supplied:** each file type named in `entity_filters` is restricted to the features its filter matches. **File types not named keep the default behaviour.**

### Matching

- `filters` is a list of **groups**. Each group is a set of `attribute: value` pairs.
- A feature matches a group when it has **all** of the group's pairs with **exactly** those values (AND within a group; exact, case-sensitive match).
- A feature is **eligible** when it matches **at least one** group (OR across groups).
- Any OSW attribute, including `ext:*` attributes, can be used in a filter.

### What eligibility controls, per file type

| File type | Only eligible features… | Ineligible features… |
|---|---|---|
| `edge` | can be removed as duplicates, and only when the DS1 edge they duplicate is **also** eligible. | are **always kept**, even when they duplicate a DS1 edge — so both copies appear in the output. They still connect (section 5). |
| `node` | have their attributes merged, and only when **both** nodes are eligible. | still join by proximity; DS2 values are recorded in `ext:union_audit_*` only. |
| `point`, `line`, `polygon`, `zone` | can be merged, and only with a feature that is **also** eligible. | are kept as they are (DS1) or added as new (DS2). |

**An edge filter also narrows node attribute merging.** A node's attributes merge only when both nodes lie on an eligible edge (and match the `node` filter, if one is given). Node **joining** is never affected.

**A filter that matches nothing does not raise an error.** Nothing of that file type is merged, and the job still completes. If the output looks unmerged, check the attribute names and values in the filter.

### Worked example — edge filter on sidewalks only

```json
{"edge": {"filters": [{"highway": "footway", "footway": "sidewalk"}]}}
```

- DS2 **sidewalks** that duplicate DS1 sidewalks are removed.
- All **other DS2 edges** (crossings, plain footways, steps, roads…) are **added**, even when they duplicate a DS1 edge.
- **All nodes still join** as described in section 5. Node attributes merge only where both nodes lie on sidewalks; everywhere else DS2 values are audited only.
- Road × crossing nodes, T-junction splits and every other step in section 5 **still run**.
- Zones, points, lines and polygons **behave as default**.

Adding a second group — `{"highway": "footway", "footway": "crossing"}` — makes sidewalks **or** crossings eligible.

### Duplicate-detection settings

These go in the same per-file-type block and can be used with or without `filters`.

| Setting | File types | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duplicate_buffer_width` | `edge`, `line` | `proximity` | Width in metres of the corridor around each DS1 edge or line. A DS2 edge or line inside it counts as covered. It is independent of `proximity`: widening it never makes more nodes join. |
| `duplicate_overlap_percentage` | `edge` | 80 | Minimum share of the DS2 edge's length inside the corridor for it to count as a duplicate. |
| | `line` | 70 | Minimum share of the DS2 line's length inside the corridor. |
| | `polygon` | 70 | Share of the DS1 polygon's area the two polygons must share to be treated as the same polygon. At or below it, intersecting polygons are combined. |
| | `zone` | 70 | Share of the DS1 zone's area the two zones must share to be treated as the same zone. |

Nodes and points are merged by `proximity` only, so neither setting applies to them.

---

## 7. Output

The job produces one OSW dataset with node, edge, zone, point, line and polygon files.

- **IDs:** DS1 features keep their IDs. DS2 features that were added keep their DS2 IDs. Road × crossing nodes get new `ixn-` IDs. **Edges are renumbered** with a new sequential `_id`; `_u_id` and `_v_id` refer to the output node IDs, and zone `_w_id` lists refer to output node IDs.
- **Added tags:**

| Tag | On | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ext:union_audit_<key>` | merged nodes and points | Every DS2 value for `<key>`, as `<ds2_id>-<value>`, comma-separated when several DS2 features merged. Kept even when DS1's value won or a filter withheld the merge. |
| `ext:union_confidence` | merged nodes | Score from 0 to 1: 0.7 × proximity score + 0.3 × type-match score. |
| `ext:union_confidence_proximity` | merged nodes | 1 − (join distance ÷ `proximity`). |
| `ext:union_confidence_type_match` | merged nodes | 1.0 when both nodes lie on the same kind of way; 0.5 when either node's way type is unknown. |
| `ext:union_confidence_source` | merged nodes | The union that produced the score, `<dataset_one>+<dataset_two>`. |
| `ext:union_confidence_status` | nodes | `merged` when scored by this union; `carried` when the score came from an earlier union and the node did not merge this time. |
| `ext:osw_*`, `ext:road_*` | `ixn-` nodes | Tags of the crossing and the road that created the node. |

- Any `ext:*` attribute that holds different JSON types on different features (for example a number on some, text on others) is output as text on all of them.

---

## 8. Validation errors (HTTP 400)

- The request body is empty, or a dataset ID is missing.
- `proximity` is not a positive number.
- `entity_filters` is not an object, or names a file type other than `edge`, `node`, `point`, `zone`, `line`, `polygon`.
- A block contains a key other than `filters`, `duplicate_buffer_width`, `duplicate_overlap_percentage`.
- `filters` is not a list.
- `duplicate_buffer_width` is not a number greater than 0, or is given for `node`, `point`, `zone` or `polygon`.
- `duplicate_overlap_percentage` is not a number greater than 0 and at most 100, or is given for `node` or `point`.

Unrecognised keys are always **rejected**, never ignored, so a typing mistake cannot produce a run that silently applies none of the request.

---

## 9. Tracking the job

The response is a `job_id`, and the `Location` header gives the status URL. Track the job with `GET /api/v1/jobs` (job type `Dataset-Union`). Once its status is `COMPLETED`, download the result with `GET /api/v1/job/download/{job_id}`.

UnionEntityFilterBlock.description: Settings for one OSW file type. Every property is optional. `filters` controls which features are eligible to merge; the `duplicate_*` settings tune when two features count as the same. None of them affect connectivity.

filters.description:
List of filter groups. A feature is **eligible to merge** when it matches **at least one** group (OR). It matches a group when it has **every** attribute/value pair in it with exactly that value (AND; exact, case-sensitive). Any OSW attribute, including `ext:*`, can be used.

Only eligible features can be removed as duplicates or have attributes merged, and only with a counterpart that is also eligible. Ineligible features are never removed: DS1 features pass through and DS2 features are added. They still connect to the network.

An empty list is the same as no filter. A filter that matches no feature is not an error; nothing of that file type is merged.

duplicate_buffer_width.description: **`edge` and `line` only.** Width in metres of the corridor around each DS1 edge or line; a DS2 edge or line lying inside it counts as covered. **Default: the request's `proximity`.** Independent of `proximity`: widening the corridor never makes more nodes join. Rejected for `node`, `point`, `zone` and `polygon`.

duplicate_overlap_percentage.description:
Minimum overlap, in percent, for two features to count as the same.

- `edge` — share of the DS2 edge's length inside the corridor. **Default 80.** The edge must also run alongside the DS1 edge (within 30°).
- `line` — share of the DS2 line's length inside the corridor. **Default 70.**
- `polygon` — share of the DS1 polygon's area the two polygons share. **Default 70.** At or below it, intersecting polygons are combined into one shape.
- `zone` — share of the DS1 zone's area the two zones share. **Default 70.**

Rejected for `node` and `point`, which merge by `proximity` only.

UnionEntityFilters.description:
Optional per-file-type merge filters and duplicate-detection settings. Keys must be OSW file types: `edge`, `node`, `point`, `zone`, `line`, `polygon`; any other key is rejected.

- **Omitted entirely:** every feature of every file type is eligible to merge.
- **A file type named:** only its features matching the filter are eligible.
- **A file type not named:** default behaviour.

Filters decide **what is merged, never what is connected**.

edge.description: Edge merging. Only eligible DS2 edges can be removed as duplicates, and only of eligible DS1 edges. Ineligible DS2 edges are always added, even when they duplicate a DS1 edge, and still connect to the network. The edge filter also narrows node attribute merging: attributes merge only when both nodes lie on eligible edges. Supports `filters`, `duplicate_buffer_width` and `duplicate_overlap_percentage` (default 80).

node.description: Node **attribute** merging. Nodes always join by `proximity` (section 5 of the union description); this filter only decides whether DS2 attributes are merged onto the joined DS1 node. Both nodes must match (and lie on an eligible edge, if an edge filter is given). Withheld DS2 values are still recorded in `ext:union_audit_*`. Supports `filters` only.

point.description: Point merging. Two points of the same type within `proximity` merge only when both match. Others are kept or added unchanged. Supports `filters` only.

zone.description: Zone merging. Two overlapping zones are treated as the same only when both match. Supports `filters` and `duplicate_overlap_percentage` (default 70).

line.description: Line merging. A DS2 line inside a DS1 line's corridor merges only when both match. Supports `filters`, `duplicate_buffer_width` and `duplicate_overlap_percentage` (default 70).

polygon.description: Polygon merging. Intersecting polygons are merged or combined only when both match; otherwise both are kept unchanged. Supports `filters` and `duplicate_overlap_percentage` (default 70).
